name: Canthal tilt tape (lateral eye lift tape)

card.summary: Tape pulled toward the temple to angle the outer eye corners upward; no studies were found.
card.aka: lateral eye lift tape, fox eye tape
card.note: No clinical research found; applied next to the eye.

quick.overview:
Canthal tilt tape is adhesive tape stuck near the outer corner of the eye and pulled back toward the temple, so the outer corner sits higher. In looksmaxxing vocabulary a more upward-angled outer corner is called positive canthal tilt.

The sources reviewed contain no studies of the tape. This entry therefore covers definitions only.
quick.mechanism: The tape holds the skin at the lateral canthus under tension, which is intended to raise the apparent position of the outer corner relative to the inner corner. The effect is temporary and ends when the tape is removed.
quick.risks: No studies of safety or effectiveness were found. Adhesive and skin tension near the eye are general considerations that have not been tested for this product.

lead: Canthal tilt tape, also called lateral eye lift tape, is a temporary cosmetic aid in which tape is attached near the outer eye corner and pulled toward the temple to alter the apparent angle of the eye. The canthi are the corners of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet; the lateral canthus is the outer corner and the medial canthus the inner corner [1].

No published clinical studies of the tape were located. In appearance forums a more upward-angled outer corner is commonly called positive canthal tilt, but the sources reviewed for this entry do not provide data on perceptions of tilt or on the tape.

paras: The canthus is the corner of the eye where the eyelids meet. Anatomical references describe the bicanthal plane through both canthi as marking the upper boundary of the midface, and note that in many East Asian eyes the inner corner is partly covered by an epicanthic fold while in other populations it is typically fully exposed [1].
